Both files written.

**Gold file:** `gold.json` (no `golden.json` in this case dir). I read `ranked.json` in full before opening it — it is a **flat single-repo array** of 75 paths, matching the shape `gold.json` uses, so no flattening was needed.

**Scorer:** `python3 score_arm.py …` ran clean; all numbers below are its output verbatim.

```
hits / gold_total   5 / 8
recall@10           0.375
recall@20           0.375
recall@25           0.375
recall@50           0.375
recall@75 (full)    0.625
precision@5         0.200
MRR                 1.000
```
score_arm.py emits only `precision@5`; it does not compute precision@10, precision@20, F1@20 or F1_full_list, and I did not hand-compute them — per the rules, substituted arithmetic would not be comparable with the rest of the series.

**found (5):**
- packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts (rank 1)
- packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/service/EmailWorkflowService.ts (rank 8)
- packages/features/bookings/lib/service/RegularBookingService.ts (rank 10)
- packages/features/tasker/tasks/sendWorkflowEmails.ts (rank 67)
- packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/types.ts (rank 71)

**missed_gold (3):**
- apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-04-15/controllers/bookings.controller.ts
- apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-08-13/services/input.service.ts
- packages/prisma/zod-utils.ts

**Surface verdict: NOT comparable.** One reason, and only one: prompt caching was enabled and warm — `cache_read=4,896,769`, `cache_creation=277,251`, so the $6.52 figure is not comparable to cold runs. Everything else is clean: the 60 calls in commands.log are all plumbline MCP tools plus 2 ToolSearch schema loads (exempt), no Bash/Read/Grep/Glob, and the retriever's own search tools did fire — stakeout 16, shakedown 2, manhunt 2, collateral_damage 24. Counts were taken from commands.log, and they happen to agree with the run's cost.json self-report.

**What the misses share:** all three sit at the API-v2 / schema boundary rather than in the workflow-email execution path the run occupied. Two are the v2 REST layer for bookings — a controller and its input service — and the third is the Prisma zod schema module. The 24 collateral_damage folds and the whole seed set stayed inside `packages/features/ee/workflows`, `packages/emails` and the booking services; the v2 app reached the list only as `booking-emails-sms-service.ts` and `workflows.repository.ts` (ranks 38, 48), i.e. the v2 files that call back into workflows, never the request-entry controller or the input-validation service above them. `packages/prisma/zod-utils.ts` is the same register one layer lower: shared validation/type plumbing, not a caller or callee of the email path. The three found-late hits (ranks 67, 71) and the three misses are the same story — the run resolved the runtime call graph confidently and the declarative type/validation edge weakly.
